actions.action: Check whether the stem base is firm or mushy and whether the leaves are soft
Take the plant out of the pot and inspect the roots
Cut off any rotted roots with clean scissors
Repot into cactus or succulent mix with extra perlite or pumice (50%+ grit)
Check that the inner pot has drainage holes and empty water from the cache pot
Bury the stem slightly deeper if it is long and bare
Wait a week after repotting, then water thoroughly only when the soil is completely dry
Place yellow sticky traps near the pot
Water with a Bti treatment (mosquito bits) to kill gnat larvae
Scrape off the moldy top layer of soil and replace it with dry grit or sand
Move the plant to a bright spot with a few hours of direct sun
If the stem is mushy when unpotted, report back for guidance on cutting off the rot and re-rooting

reason: The answer correctly identifies the overly wet soil, mold and gnats but treats rot only as a conditional possibility and suggests it may have been caught early; its repotting into cactus mix and root trimming match much of the fix, but chopping off the rotten part is deferred to a follow-up, and nothing in it is likely to harm the plant.
